sentences.en: One year ago tomorrow, an unfathomable scene played out at the U.S.
sentences.zh: 明天是一年前的今天，美国国会大厦上演了令人难以置信的

sentences.en: Capitol.
sentences.zh: 一幕。

sentences.en: — Madam Speaker, members of Congress, pursuant to the Constitution and the laws of the United States, the Senate and House of Representatives are meeting in joint session.
sentences.zh: ——议长女士，各位国会议员，根据美国宪法和法律，参议院和众议院正在举行联席会议。

sentences.en: — That morning, Congress was scheduled to certify the results of the 2020 election, making Joe Biden the next president of the United States.
sentences.zh: ——那天早上，国会原定认证2020年大选结果，使乔·拜登成为下一任美国总统。

sentences.en: For weeks, Donald Trump and his allies had been working to subvert those results, pressuring state and local election officials, submitting lawsuit after lawsuit,
sentences.zh: 数周以来，唐纳德·特朗普及其盟友一直试图推翻这些结果，向州和地方选举官员施压，接连提起诉讼，

sentences.en: and calling on the vice president himself not to perform his constitutional duty in certifying Biden's victory.
sentences.zh: 并呼吁副总统本人不要履行其认证拜登胜选的宪法职责。

sentences.en: All of that had failed.
sentences.zh: 所有这些努力都失败了。

sentences.en: And so on January 6th...
sentences.zh: 于是，在1月6日那天……

sentences.en: Our country has been under siege for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我们的国家长期以来一直处于围困之中。

sentences.en: President Trump went to the National Mall.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统去了国家广场。

sentences.en: And you're the real people.
sentences.zh: 你们才是真正的人民。

sentences.en: You're the people that built this nation.
sentences.zh: 你们是建设这个国家的人民。

sentences.en: and urged the thousands of Americans who had gathered there to march on the Capitol and, quote,
sentences.zh: 并敦促聚集在那里的成千上万名美国人向国会大厦进军，引用他的话：

sentences.en: We fight.
sentences.zh: 我们要战斗。

sentences.en: We fight like hell.
sentences.zh: 我们要拼命战斗。

sentences.en: Fight like hell.
sentences.zh: 拼命战斗。

sentences.en: And if you don't fight like hell, you're not going to have a country anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你不拼命战斗，你就不会再拥有这个国家了。

sentences.en: And so,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: We are going to the Capitol, where our problems are.
sentences.zh: 我们要去国会大厦，那里才是我们问题所在的地方。

sentences.en: The country watched as scenes of chaos and violence
sentences.zh: 全国人民目睹了混乱和暴力的场面

sentences.en: Fight for Trump!
sentences.zh: 为特朗普而战！

sentences.en: Fight for Trump!
sentences.zh: 为特朗普而战！

sentences.en: Played out in the halls of government.
sentences.zh: 在政府大厅里上演。

sentences.en: As rioters flooded through the doors.
sentences.zh: 暴徒们涌入了大门。

sentences.en: Members of Congress were rushed to safety.
sentences.zh: 国会议员们被紧急转移到安全地带。

sentences.en: And American citizens engaged in hand-to-hand combat with Capitol Police.
sentences.zh: 美国公民与国会警察发生了肉搏战。

sentences.en: Ultimately, 150 law enforcement officials were injured.
sentences.zh: 最终，150名执法人员受伤。

sentences.en: And five people were left dead.
sentences.zh: 五人死亡。

sentences.en: The government did this to us.
sentences.zh: 政府对我们做了这种事。

sentences.en: We were normal, good, law-abiding citizens.
sentences.zh: 我们原本是正常、善良、守法的公民。

sentences.en: And you guys did this to us.
sentences.zh: 而你们这些人对我们做了这种事。

sentences.en: We want our country back.
sentences.zh: 我们要夺回我们的国家。

sentences.en: Today, we begin a three-part look at what happened that day and what it tells us about the state of American democracy.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们开始分三部分回顾那天发生的事情，以及它向我们揭示了美国民主的现状。

sentences.en: In part one, my colleague Alan Foyer reports on what we've learned about who the rioters actually were and takes us inside an FBI interview with one of them.
sentences.zh: 在第一部分中，我的同事艾伦·福耶尔报道了我们对暴徒真实身份的了解，并带我们深入了解了FBI对其中一人的审讯过程。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 5th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月5日，星期三。

sentences.en: Alan, we are going to do something a bit different today.
sentences.zh: 艾伦，我们今天要做点不一样的。

sentences.en: We're going to dive with you into the transcript of an FBI interrogation with a January 6th participant.
sentences.zh: 我们将和你一起深入研究一份FBI对一名1月6日参与者的审讯笔录。

sentences.en: And before we do that, I want to talk about why this feels so important to us.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，我想谈谈为什么这件事对我们来说如此重要。

sentences.en: Let's start by talking about what you have been doing in the year since January 6th?
sentences.zh: 首先，请谈谈你在1月6日之后的一年里都在做什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I have more or less been singularly consumed by the question of who was part of that mob.
sentences.zh: 我几乎全身心地投入到研究那个暴徒群体到底是由谁组成的这个问题上。

sentences.en: From the beginning, there's been a focus on whether there was any real organization on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，人们就关注1月6日那天是否存在真正的组织策划。

sentences.en: And much of the attention has been on the presence of far-right extremists, people from groups like the Proud Boys and the Oath Keepers.
sentences.zh: 大部分注意力都集中在极右翼极端分子的存在上，比如“骄傲男孩”和“誓言守护者”等组织的成员。

sentences.en: Obviously, the authorities have also been intensely interested in anyone who attacked police officers, anyone who engaged in clear-cut violence.
sentences.zh: 显然，当局也对任何袭击警察的人、任何参与了明确暴力行为的人非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: You know, those were the people we saw throwing fire extinguishers or beating officers with crutches and hockey sticks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是我们看到的那些扔灭火器，或者用拐杖和曲棍球棒殴打警察的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there was a whole other group of people that, at least from what we saw that day, seemed to be different.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一大群人，至少从我们那天看到的情况来看，似乎有所不同。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These were the people who almost appeared to have wandered into the building, who were walking around, taking pictures of the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 这些人看起来几乎像是误打误撞进了大楼，他们四处走动，给国会大厦拍照。

sentences.en: You know, some of them were live streaming themselves as they posed in front of statues and Congress members' offices.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人甚至在雕像和国会议员办公室前摆姿势时还在进行直播。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember that vividly because it was one of the most unexpected images of that day.
sentences.zh: 我对此记忆犹新，因为那是那天最出人意料的画面之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Even though it seemed like they weren't doing all that much, they were part of the mob.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们看起来没做什么过分的事，但他们确实是暴徒的一员。

sentences.en: And the fact is, without their collective physical presence, January 6th doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 事实是，如果没有他们集体的身体在场，1月6日的事件就不会发生。

sentences.en: As the government itself has said in countless sentencing documents from January 6th, a riot cannot occur without rioters.
sentences.zh: 正如政府自己在1月6日无数份量刑文件中所说的那样，没有暴徒，就不会发生暴乱。

sentences.en: And they point out that each rioter's actions, from the most mundane to the most violent, contributed directly and indirectly to the violence and destruction of that day.
sentences.zh: 他们指出，每位暴徒的行为，从最琐碎的到最暴力的，都直接或间接地促成了那天的暴力和破坏。

sentences.en: Still, you know, individually, these people don't fit the mold of the classic far-right extremists.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，你知道，从个人来看，这些人并不符合典型的极右翼极端分子的形象。

sentences.en: And so it's felt to me that understanding who those people are and what brought them to that day, that's a very important part of understanding sort of what the hell happened
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，了解这些人是谁，是什么让他们在那天来到那里，对于理解到底发生了什么非常重要，

sentences.en: and what it says about this state of our democracy.
sentences.zh: 以及它对我们民主现状意味着什么。

sentences.en: Which of our fellow Americans showed up and why?
sentences.zh: 到底是哪些美国同胞出现在了那里，为什么？

sentences.en: And what have we learned about that?
sentences.zh: 我们对此了解到了什么？

sentences.en: Well, an interesting portrait has emerged of the more than 700 people who have been charged so far.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到目前为止被起诉的700多人中，出现了一幅有趣的画像。

sentences.en: Just one in 10 was a member of a far-right extremist group.
sentences.zh: 只有十分之一的人是极右翼极端组织的成员。

sentences.en: 12% had a military background.
sentences.zh: 12%的人有军事背景。

sentences.en: More than half either had white-collar jobs or owned their own businesses.
sentences.zh: 超过一半的人要么从事白领工作，要么拥有自己的企业。

sentences.en: There were doctors, lawyers, substitute teachers, church deacons.
sentences.zh: 其中有医生、律师、代课老师、教堂执事。

sentences.en: There was a State Department official.
sentences.zh: 还有一名国务院官员。

sentences.en: And in terms of where they came from, where in the country, it doesn't really map neatly onto much of anything.
sentences.zh: 至于他们来自哪里，全国各地都有，并没有明显的规律可循。

sentences.en: In fact, if someone lived in a county that Trump won in the 2020 election, they were less likely to be there than if they lived in a county won by Biden.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果一个人住在特朗普在2020年大选中获胜的县，他们出现在那里的可能性反而比住在拜登获胜的县的人要低。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And many of these people, they described themselves and were described by people who know them as good neighbors, churchgoers, community leaders.
sentences.zh: 这些人中的许多人，他们自己描述，以及认识他们的人描述，都是好邻居、常去教堂的人、社区领袖。

sentences.en: A lot of them had never been particularly political in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人过去从未表现出特别的政治倾向。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Until, it seems, this day.
sentences.zh: 直到这一天，似乎才有所改变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, why were they there?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们为什么会在那里？

sentences.en: And honestly, it's been hard to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 老实说，很难回答这个问题。

sentences.en: You know, I've tried to talk to as many of the people who were there that day as I can, but for obvious reasons,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我尽量去采访那天在场的人，但出于显而易见的原因，

sentences.en: people who are charged with a crime don't often find it in their best interest to talk openly with journalists.
sentences.zh: 被指控犯罪的人通常认为与记者公开交谈并不符合他们的最大利益。

sentences.en: I mean, also, there's just really no single answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个问题确实没有单一的答案。

sentences.en: And so the most expansive look at these people that we have happens to come from three FBI interviews that have been released to the public.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们对这些人最详尽的了解来自于已向公众发布的三份FBI审讯记录。

sentences.en: There were hundreds of these interviews done, but for legal reasons, only three have seen the light of day.
sentences.zh: 这类审讯进行了数百次，但出于法律原因，只有三份得以公开。

sentences.en: And they really do give you an intricate sense of some of the people who were there that day from their own perspective.
sentences.zh: 它们确实让你从当事人的视角，对那天在场的一些人有了深刻的了解。

sentences.en: And the most revealing of those interviews to me is from a man named
sentences.zh: 而在我看来，其中最能揭示真相的采访来自一个名叫

sentences.en: Robert Reeder.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·里德的人。

sentences.en: At the time of the interview, Reeder was facing four misdemeanor charges for entering the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 在接受采访时，里德因进入国会大厦面临四项轻罪指控。

sentences.en: And as his sentencing approached, Reeder's lawyer made the decision to release the transcript of the interview he did with the FBI.
sentences.zh: 随着量刑临近，里德的律师决定公布他接受FBI采访的笔录。

sentences.en: Right, and all of that explains what we are up to today.
sentences.zh: 没错，所有这些都解释了我们今天要做的事情。

sentences.en: Given the journalistic value of this FBI interview, and because the recording of the interview was not released along with the transcript,
sentences.zh: 鉴于这份FBI审讯记录的新闻价值，且采访录音并未随笔录一同发布，

sentences.en: we're going to do something, as we said, unusual.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，我们将做一件不同寻常的事。

sentences.en: We have worked with voice actors to bring that transcript to life.
sentences.zh: 我们与配音演员合作，将这份笔录呈现出来。

sentences.en: The only editing we have done is for length and for clarity because the original interview was more than 100 pages long.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一的编辑是为了篇幅和清晰度，因为原始采访长达100多页。

sentences.en: And, Alan, as we're listening, what do you think it's important that people keep in mind about the nature of an FBI interrogation, especially in a case like this?
sentences.zh: 艾伦，在我们听的时候，你认为人们在了解FBI审讯的性质时，尤其是在这种案件中，应该记住什么？

sentences.en: Well, one thing to keep in mind is that the FBI already knows a lot about Robert Reeder.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一点要记住，FBI已经对罗伯特·里德了解很多了。

sentences.en: He actually voluntarily turned himself into law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是主动向执法部门自首的。

sentences.en: And as part of that, he handed over lots of photographs and video that he himself took that day.
sentences.zh: 作为配合的一部分，他交出了许多他自己在那天拍摄的照片和视频。

sentences.en: So the agents have all that.
sentences.zh: 所以探员们已经掌握了所有这些资料。

sentences.en: They also know his biography.
sentences.zh: 他们也了解他的个人背景。

sentences.en: Reeder is in his mid-50s.
sentences.zh: 里德五十多岁。

sentences.en: He's a FedEx driver from suburban Maryland, or he was a FedEx driver at the time of the insurrection.
sentences.zh: 他是马里兰州郊区的一名联邦快递司机，或者说在暴乱发生时他是联邦快递司机。

sentences.en: He's single, and he has a son.
sentences.zh: 他单身，有一个儿子。

sentences.en: The agents have seen his social media.
sentences.zh: 探员们查看了他的社交媒体。

sentences.en: They know he was a member of multiple pro-Trump groups on Facebook, though he claims to be a lifelong Democrat.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他是Facebook上多个支持特朗普群组的成员，尽管他声称自己是终身民主党人。

sentences.en: He posted memes about the voter fraud myth.
sentences.zh: 他发布过关于选民欺诈神话的迷因。

sentences.en: He wrote that, quote, civil war is coming.
sentences.zh: 他写道，引用他的话，“内战即将来临”。

sentences.en: And that, again, this is a quote, this time the conservatives will stand their ground and the radicals will die.
sentences.zh: 而且，再次引用他的话，“这一次保守派将坚守阵地，激进分子将会死亡”。

sentences.en: But again, like most of the people there, he doesn't have a violent history or any ties to far right group.
sentences.zh: 但同样，像大多数在场的人一样，他没有暴力史，也没有与极右翼组织有任何联系。

sentences.en: So the FBI agents are less interested in what he did, which they think they know, and they're more interested in why and how he did it.
sentences.zh: 所以FBI探员对他的所作所为兴趣不大（因为他们认为自己已经知道了），他们更感兴趣的是他为什么以及如何做这些事。

sentences.en: And for his part, Reeder certainly has his own agenda.
sentences.zh: 而就里德而言，他当然也有自己的打算。

sentences.en: He and his lawyer are in that room essentially to do what they can to diminish his exposure to criminal punishment, which means that it may not be in his interest to
sentences.zh: 他和他的律师坐在那个房间里，本质上是为了尽其所能减少他面临的刑事处罚，这意味着他可能并不想

sentences.en: be entirely forthcoming about what happened that day.
sentences.zh: 完全坦白那天发生的事情。

sentences.en: So there's definitely some cat and mouse going on.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一场猫鼠游戏。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And finally, Alan, can you set the scene for us for this interview?
sentences.zh: 最后，艾伦，你能为我们介绍一下这次采访的背景吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: We are in the FBI field office in Baltimore, Maryland, and we've got two FBI agents.
sentences.zh: 我们在马里兰州巴尔的摩的FBI外勤办公室，有两名FBI探员。

sentences.en: We've got Robert Reader himself, and we've got his attorney.
sentences.zh: 还有罗伯特·里德本人，以及他的律师。

sentences.en: And they're sitting in what is presumably a small conference room talking across a table.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在一个大概是小型会议室的地方，隔着桌子交谈。

sentences.en: You don't happen to have a Kleenex, do you?
sentences.zh: 你手头没有纸巾吧？

sentences.en: We could grab some tissues out of the restroom if you'd like some for you, sir.
sentences.zh: 如果您需要的话，我们可以去洗手间给您拿些纸巾，先生。

sentences.en: Nah, I just, just let me know if at any point, let me know, I'll step out and get it.
sentences.zh: 不用，我只是……如果需要的话我会告诉你们，我会出去拿的。

sentences.en: All right, gotcha.
sentences.zh: 好的，明白了。

sentences.en: All right, so I'm just gonna start a preamble.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我就先做一个开场白。

sentences.en: So my name is Special Agent Alexandria Thoman.
sentences.zh: 我是特别探员亚历山大·托曼。

sentences.en: I'm here with Special Agent Hunter Locke.
sentences.zh: 我和特别探员亨特·洛克在一起。

sentences.en: If you wouldn't mind stating your name for the record.
sentences.zh: 如果不介意的话，请报一下您的名字以作记录。

sentences.en: Robert Reeder.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·里德。

sentences.en: Great.

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Okay, Alan, let me try to sum up that interrogation.
sentences.zh: 好的，艾伦，让我试着总结一下那次审讯。

sentences.en: By his telling, Robert Reeder is a single father, a FedEx worker who, driven by some combination of boredom, questions about the election,
sentences.zh: 据他所说，罗伯特·里德是一位单身父亲，一名联邦快递员工，在无聊、对选举的质疑，

sentences.en: and in part his simple geographic proximity to Washington, makes his way with the crowd to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 以及部分因为他地理位置上离华盛顿很近的共同驱动下，他随人群前往了美国

sentences.en: Capitol on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 国会大厦，时间是1月6日。

sentences.en: Once inside, he says he pretty quickly wants to find his way out of the Capitol, but then is unable to explain why he goes back into the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 进入后，他说他很快就想找到离开国会大厦的路，但随后无法解释为什么他又回到了国会大厦。

sentences.en: He insists that he didn't understand the intention of some in the mob that day to block Congress from certifying Biden's election victory.
sentences.zh: 他坚称自己不了解那天暴徒中一些人阻止国会认证拜登选举胜利的意图。

sentences.en: He says he's sickened by their actions, wants them held accountable.
sentences.zh: 他说他对他们的行为感到恶心，希望他们被追究责任。

sentences.en: He expresses remorse, and the FBI investigators tell him that they believe him.
sentences.zh: 他表达了悔意，联邦调查局的调查人员告诉他，他们相信他。

sentences.en: So, ultimately, what do you make of Reeder's account?
sentences.zh: 那么，归根结底，你如何看待里德的陈述？

sentences.en: Is this typical?
sentences.zh: 这典型吗？

sentences.en: Actually, it is.
sentences.zh: 事实上，是的。

sentences.en: In my reporting, I found that what Reeder's saying is really not that unusual at all.
sentences.zh: 在我的报道中，我发现里德所说的情况一点也不罕见。

sentences.en: a lot of people have this same story.
sentences.zh: 很多人都有同样的故事。

sentences.en: They say they were going with the herd.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们只是随大流。

sentences.en: They say they were truly remorseful about what happened.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们对发生的事情真的感到后悔。

sentences.en: They talk about the devastating impact it's had on their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了这对他们的生活造成的毁灭性影响。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's entirely possible that many of them do feel that way.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们中很多人确实有这种感觉，这是完全可能的。

sentences.en: You know, but it's also the case that every participant in January 6th would have an interest in talking about themselves like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但事实也确实是，每一位参与1月6日事件的人，都有动机那样描述自己。

sentences.en: The passerby, the hapless participant, the person who was more motivated by curiosity than by any driving ideology or desire to violently overturn an election.
sentences.zh: 路人、倒霉的参与者，比起任何驱动性的意识形态或暴力推翻选举的欲望，更多是出于好奇心而行动的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But is it true?
sentences.zh: 但这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We already knew from Reeder's social media that he had grown more extreme in his political beliefs than he's portraying to the FBI in this interview.
sentences.zh: 我们从里德的社交媒体上已经知道，他的政治信仰比他在这次采访中向联邦调查局描述的要激进得多。

sentences.en: But after the interview, there's actually a new piece of evidence that emerges that challenges Reeder's account and further complicates the image that he's putting forward.
sentences.zh: 但在采访之后，实际上出现了一项新的证据，挑战了里德的说法，并使他所呈现的形象进一步复杂化。

sentences.en: And what is that new information?
sentences.zh: 那是什么新信息？

sentences.en: So four months after Reeder is interrogated by the FBI, he's scheduled for his sentencing hearing in front of a federal judge in Washington.
sentences.zh: 在里德接受联邦调查局审讯四个月后，他被安排在华盛顿的一位联邦法官面前进行量刑听证会。

sentences.en: But literally just a few hours before the sentencing starts, a new video of Reeder from January 6th emerges.
sentences.zh: 但就在量刑开始前几个小时，一段里德在1月6日当天的新视频出现了。

sentences.en: It's actually dug up by this group of amateur online detectives who have been helping track down participants in January 6th.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是由一群一直在帮助追踪1月6日参与者的业余网络侦探挖掘出来的。

sentences.en: They call themselves sedition hunters.
sentences.zh: 他们自称为“煽动叛乱猎人”。

sentences.en: And this new footage, it shows Reeder in an altercation with a police officer.
sentences.zh: 这段新录像显示里德与一名警官发生了冲突。

sentences.en: And so what do you see in that video?
sentences.zh: 那么你在那段视频中看到了什么？

sentences.en: So you actually see the scene that Reeder was describing to the agents during his interview.
sentences.zh: 你实际上看到了里德在采访中向探员描述的那个场景。

sentences.en: You know, he's kind of described this event as a police officer falling on top of him in the chaos of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他把这件事描述为在混乱中一名警官倒在他身上。

sentences.en: And, you know, he helps the officer back up onto his feet.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他帮那名警官站了起来。

sentences.en: But in the video, you just see Reeder in a much more confrontational position towards the cop.
sentences.zh: 但在视频中，你看到的只是里德对警察采取了更具对抗性的姿态。

sentences.en: You know, it's this kind of confusing melee of pushing and shoving, but it just looks a lot more like an altercation than what Reeder had described to the FBI.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是一场混乱的推搡，但看起来比里德向联邦调查局描述的情况更像是一场冲突。

sentences.en: So this video establishes what sure looks like a discrepancy between what actually happened and what Reeder wants the FBI to think.
sentences.zh: 所以这段视频确立了事实真相与里德想让联邦调查局相信的情况之间明显的出入。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So what happens after this video surfaces?
sentences.zh: 那么这段视频浮出水面后发生了什么？

sentences.en: So something kind of unusual.
sentences.zh: 发生了一件有点不寻常的事。

sentences.en: The sentencing hearing that was supposed to go off that day is actually called off, and it's delayed two months so that both sides can review the video.
sentences.zh: 原定于当天进行的量刑听证会被取消了，并推迟了两个月，以便双方都能查看这段视频。

sentences.en: And in the end, the Justice Department decides to stick with the original misdemeanor charges.
sentences.zh: 最终，司法部决定维持最初的轻罪指控。

sentences.en: They're not going to charge Reeder with anything additional like assault.
sentences.zh: 他们不会对里德追加任何像袭击罪之类的指控。

sentences.en: But what they do is that they ask that his sentence be increased from the two months they had originally requested to six months.
sentences.zh: 但他们所做的是要求将他的刑期从最初要求的两个月增加到六个月。

sentences.en: During the hearing, the judge actually notes the discrepancies in Reeder's account.
sentences.zh: 在听证会上，法官确实指出了里德陈述中的矛盾之处。

sentences.en: And he says that some of Reeder's statements to law enforcement were, quote, disingenuous and self-serving.
sentences.zh: 他说里德对执法部门的一些陈述是，引用他的话，“虚伪且自私的”。

sentences.en: And that, quote, it's rewriting history and the facts to say you didn't know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 并且，引用他的话，“说你不知道发生了什么，这是在改写历史和事实”。

sentences.en: I've had too many people say that to me.
sentences.zh: 我有太多人对我这么说了。

sentences.en: By which he means too many January 6th participants.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是太多1月6日的参与者都这么说。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, Reeder, for his part, apologizes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，里德本人对此表示道歉。

sentences.en: And he calls the riot disgusting.
sentences.zh: 他称那场骚乱令人作呕。

sentences.en: He calls his own actions shameful and inexcusable.
sentences.zh: 他称自己的行为是可耻且不可原谅的。

sentences.en: The judge acknowledges that Reeder appears remorseful.
sentences.zh: 法官承认里德看起来确实有悔意。

sentences.en: And ultimately, he kind of splits the difference, and he sentenced his reader to three months in jail.
sentences.zh: 最终，他折中了一下，判处里德三个月监禁。

sentences.en: Three months for participating in the storming of the Capitol on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 因参与1月6日冲击国会大厦而被判三个月。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at it overall, January 6th has—it's just been a strange case for prosecutors because for about half of the participants charged so far,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你从整体上看，1月6日事件对检察官来说一直是一个奇怪的案件，因为到目前为止被起诉的参与者中，大约有一半，

sentences.en: the ones who didn't engage in the more overt acts of violence or conspiracy, you know, they're ultimately being charged with what amounts to trespassing or disorderly conduct.
sentences.zh: 那些没有参与更明显的暴力行为或阴谋的人，你知道，他们最终被指控的只是非法入侵或扰乱治安。

sentences.en: Despite the fact that there are likely many of them like Reeder,
sentences.zh: 尽管事实上他们中可能有很多人像里德一样，

sentences.en: for whom the line between quote-unquote hapless participant and wanderer and someone capable of real violence seems actually pretty thin.
sentences.zh: 对于他们来说，所谓的“倒霉参与者”、“漫游者”与有能力实施真正暴力的人之间的界限似乎确实非常模糊。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And I think that's precisely why I've been consumed by this story and by the question of who was in the mob.
sentences.zh: 我认为这正是为什么我一直沉迷于这个故事，以及暴徒中到底都是些什么人的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, Eric, I'll share with you one of the most shocking facts about the people who were there on January 6th.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，埃里克，我要和你分享一个关于1月6日在场人员最令人震惊的事实。

sentences.en: By and large, the people who acted most violently that day were actually the ones who had the least violent backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，那天表现最暴力的人，实际上是那些背景最不暴力的人。

sentences.en: The people who acted the most violently on January 6th were the least likely to have had a history of violence.
sentences.zh: 在1月6日表现最暴力的人，最不可能有暴力史。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 那是对的。

sentences.en: The people who were charged with violent assaults on police officers, the ones wielding hatchets and using fire extinguishers, only a very,
sentences.zh: 那些被指控暴力袭击警察的人，那些挥舞斧头和使用灭火器的人，只有极，

sentences.en: very tiny fraction of them had any connection at all to right-wing extremist groups.
sentences.zh: 极小一部分人与右翼极端组织有任何联系。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, so in other words, even among 200 plus people who are charged with serious assaults that day, they too are in many cases not people that we understood to be a threat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，换句话说，即使在当天被指控严重袭击的200多人中，他们在很多情况下也不是我们所认为的威胁。

sentences.en: They too are the neighbors and the churchgoers and the people who serve this country.
sentences.zh: 他们也是邻居、教堂常客和为这个国家服务的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's why I and others have been calling this a mass radicalization of quote-unquote ordinary Americans.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就是为什么我和其他人一直称之为所谓的“普通美国人”的大规模激进化。

sentences.en: You know, for the last few months, I've been talking to a
sentences.zh: 你知道，过去几个月里，我一直在和一位

sentences.en: University of Chicago professor.
sentences.zh: 芝加哥大学的教授交谈。

sentences.en: He studies extremist threats and terrorism.
sentences.zh: 他研究极端主义威胁和恐怖主义。

sentences.en: And he has been pouring over the data from January 6th and trying to figure out what we can learn about who was there.
sentences.zh: 他一直在仔细研究1月6日的数据，试图弄清楚我们能从在场人员身上学到什么。

sentences.en: And one of the things that he is most alarmed by is the emergence of this huge number
sentences.zh: 他最感到震惊的事情之一是出现了如此庞大数量的

sentences.en: of Americans who don't fit the profile of typical extremists, but who believe that the election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 美国人，他们不符合典型极端分子的特征，但他们相信选举被窃取了。

sentences.en: He estimates that 21 million Americans say they believe that Trump won, that Biden lost,
sentences.zh: 他估计有2100万美国人表示他们相信特朗普赢了，拜登输了，

sentences.en: and that violence is justified to return Trump to the office they believe rightfully belongs to him.
sentences.zh: 并且认为暴力是合理的，可以使特朗普回到他们认为理应属于他的职位上。

sentences.en: 21 million Americans.
sentences.zh: 2100万美国人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you put all this together, and what does it tell you?
sentences.zh: 所以你把这一切放在一起，它告诉你什么？

sentences.en: You know, what it says is that if there's ever going to be another January 6th, or something that resembles January 6th,
sentences.zh: 你知道，它说明的是，如果未来还会发生另一次1月6日事件，或者类似1月6日的事件，

sentences.en: it most likely is not ultimately going to be because of far-right extremists or people with violent histories.
sentences.zh: 最有可能的最终原因将不会是因为极右翼极端分子或有暴力历史的人。

sentences.en: It's going to be because of people like Robert Reeder, people who harbor some sense of doubt or anger or resentment and, for whatever reason, decide to show up
sentences.zh: 那将是因为像罗伯特·里德这样的人，那些怀有某种怀疑、愤怒或怨恨，并且无论出于什么原因，决定出现

sentences.en: and become just part of the herd.
sentences.zh: 并成为群体一部分的人。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Well, thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Now, I don't know who's in charge, but somebody better do something because there are cars and families just trapped here.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不知道谁负责，但最好有人采取行动，因为这里有汽车和家庭被困住了。
